title: Hermetic CD pipeline: fingerprint gating and safe profile release
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Background:
We currently build model artifacts and publish performance profiles in the same pipeline. This coupling creates a few operational problems: a flaky integration test can block profile publication even when the binary is healthy, and a single signed artifact blob cannot be safely promoted across multiple release channels without re-signing or complex pin metadata.

Goal:
Create a hermetic, reproducible CD pipeline that separates: (1) deterministic model artifact builds (hermetic build + cryptographic fingerprint), (2) automated verification gates that operate against the fingerprint (unit/eval/perf), and (3) decoupled profile publishing that can be promoted independently while preserving provenance and auditability. The pipeline should produce an immutable signed manifest that downstream systems can consume to pin versions and enable safe roll-forward/rollback.

Design summary (high level):
- Hermetic build stage: create containerized, cache-controlled build that emits a deterministic artifact.tar.gz and a canonical fingerprint (SHA256) computed over a canonical packaging layout. Build runs in ephemeral workers and writes artifacts to the artifacts-bucket/staging/<fingerprint>/
- Signing and provenance: a signing job picks up the artifact and produces a signed-manifest.json that bundles fingerprint, build metadata (git sha, build image id, build args), and an S3-stored artifact path. Signatures are generated with KMS-backed keys and a notary-style envelope.
- Fingerprint gating jobs: independent verification jobs subscribe to the signed-manifest and run evaluations: runtime smoke, latency bench with synthetic traces, and a small regression eval against representative prompts. Each job records a verdict and a numeric score to the release dashboard.
- Profile publishing: performance profiles (batching/quant/kv-cache recommendations) are generated by a profile-producer job that references only the fingerprint. Profiles are stored in profile-catalog/<model>/<fingerprint>/profile.yaml and are not published to the public catalog until promoted. Promotion copies the profile to pinned-catalog/<model>/pinned/<version> with an entry that references the fingerprint and the signed-manifest id.
- Promotion orchestration: a promotion controller enforces policies: automatic promotion when all verification gates pass and score deltas are within thresholds; canary promotion route that publishes to 5% of hosts; manual approval path for high-impact models. Controller writes audit logs and exposes a rollback handle that points to previous pinned entry.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deterministic build reproducibility: given the same source sha and build config, repeated builds produce identical fingerprints 95%+ of the time in CI.
- Signed manifest emitted and verifiable by KMS public key.
- Verification gate jobs execute automatically and post verdicts to release dashboard within 20 minutes of build completion.
- Profile publishing is decoupled: profile-producer can generate profiles from any fingerprinted artifact and promotion is a separate operation that writes to pinned-catalog with audit metadata.
- Promotion controller supports automatic, canary (5%), and manual flows with easy rollback to previous fingerprint.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Proof-of-concept hermetic build + fingerprint (2 weeks): containerized builder, canonical pack, compute SHA256, store artifact to staging/<fp>/artifact.tar.gz. (Branch: feat/hermetic-build)
2) Signing service integration (1 week): KMS sign, signed-manifest schema, store manifest and signature in manifests/<fp>.json.
3) Gate runner (2 weeks): create verification jobs (smoke, bench, regression) that consume manifest and post verdicts to dashboard.
4) Profile-producer decoupling (2 weeks): refactor producer to read fingerprint manifest and write to profile-catalog/<model>/<fp>/profile.yaml.
5) Promotion controller & UI hooks (2 weeks): implement policy engine, canary rollout, audit logging, and a small console panel for approvals.
6) End-to-end runbook + docs + security review (1 week): update onboarding playbook, threat model, and obtain SRE/security signoff.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Start with non-customer-facing open-source models (low risk) to validate pipelines.
- Phase 2: Migrate internal test models and enable automated promotion for models that meet perf/regression SLOs.
- Phase 3: Opt-in program for customer models with manual approval requirement and stricter thresholds.

Monitoring and metrics:
- Build reproducibility ratio, gating pass rate, time-to-verdict, profile-gen latency, promotion success/failure rate, canary error rate. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/model-lifecycle/engr/41213 (placeholder).

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Deterministic builds increase complexity (tooling and caching). We accept longer initial engineering effort to avoid later flakiness in promotion.
- Signed manifests introduce key management overhead; leverage KMS + key rotation policies to mitigate risk.
- Decoupling profile publishing could produce more profile variants; we will add de-dup and pruning jobs to keep catalog manageable.
